# Getting in

Everything runs on your own laptop. Nothing leaves it. That is a feature,
and it is the same arrangement you will want at home with real data.

## RStudio Desktop

1. Open the project: double-click `IR-Quarto-Workshop.Rproj`.
2. Files pane (bottom right): `setup/00_install_packages.R`. Click **Source**. Wait for "Done".
3. `setup/01_check_setup.R`. Click **Source**. Ends with "Ready" or tells you what to fix.
4. `exercises/00_hello.qmd`. Click **Render**. A web page opens. You are in.

If step 1 fails because the laptop will not let you install R or RStudio,
raise a hand. You will pair with a neighbor for the morning and leave with
your institution's report already rendered.

*For reference only:* Posit also offers RStudio in a browser, Posit Cloud,
with nothing to install. We do not use it today. It is a hosted service on
servers your institution does not control, with no FERPA agreement unless
your institution has made one, so it is not a place for student records.

**Your UNITID:** \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ (it is in the email; or search `data/institutions.csv` by name)

**An AI assistant you can log into:** ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, Gemini. Any.

**If you are already in:** turn to exercise 1 and start. Do not wait.

## What you will leave with

An IPEDS question answered from a data set in a file that documents
itself. A report about your own institution built from the Department of
Education's 2026 Program Performance Data, the preview of the earnings
accountability results that become official in February 2027. Both
improved by an AI you drove. And an outline of the report you actually
owe someone, ready to fill.

# Why

**The problem.** More reports, more evidence, more dashboards, more
documentation. Same people. The production model has to change, not the
hours.

**The idea.** Put the query, the code, the explanation, the tables, the
charts, and the output format in one plain-text file. Render it. Version
it. Hand it over. Re-run it next year.

**The principle.** *The logic is readable; the data never is.* Everything
about how a number is made lives in a file anyone can read, including an AI.
Student records stay in the system of record and are read at render time.

## The landscape, and why RStudio

| Where people are | Good at | Weak at |
|---|---|---|
| Excel, Access | one-off answers, familiarity | repetition, history, logic hidden in cells |
| Qlik, Tableau, Power BI | dashboards, drill-down | narrative, PDFs, documentation, version control; licensed per seat |
| SAS, SPSS, Stata | scripted analysis | the report is still assembled by hand; licensed |
| Jupyter, Colab, Databricks | Python exploration | publishing; Quarto renders notebooks too |
| VS Code, Positron | multi-language IDEs | newer; Positron is Posit's next IDE, worth watching |
| **RStudio Desktop** | free, stable, Quarto built in, one-button render, the IR community | needs an install |
| Posit Cloud | RStudio in a browser, nothing to install | hosted outside your institution; not for student records; not used today |
| Posit Workbench and Connect | the server versions: shared, scheduled, published | enterprise licenses |

## What Auburn built

**High school feedback reports.** Every year, one Access report printed as
a single PDF of more than 3,500 pages, cut by hand into more than 360
files, each named by hand. Now one Quarto template, one parameter, and a
loop: 360 PDFs with the right names in one run. The rules were read out of
the Access logic and written down before anything was re-implemented, and
the old and new were run on the same year and compared figure by figure.

**Parent portal retention.** A Quarto HTML report for Student Affairs on
the office's portal, behind campus sign-in, visible only to the people
whose role allows it. The same tool that made the PDFs makes a web page;
the portal decides who sees it.

**College of Agriculture major changes.** Heatmaps on a rolling ten-cohort
window that advances by itself each August, with an "about the data" box
that states the cohort range and is generated, not typed. A report that
updates itself and documents itself.

**Faculty salary survey.** Twenty-two years in Access: about forty saved
queries run by hand in order, a hire date typed into one of them each
year, last year's table name typed into another, ten report layouts with
hand-edited headers. Underneath, about four rules and thirty-five pieces
of scaffolding that existed because Access cannot group and pivot in one
query, hold two years in one table, or remember a date. Now four tables
and fifteen views, year as a column, nothing updated in place, and one
Quarto file that prints all ten reports with the year as a parameter. On
the first run it matched the published report to the dollar on 79 of 82
lines.

**Department data packets.** One PDF per academic department: five years
of enrollment, degrees, retention, major changes, faculty, teaching,
grades, applications, in the office's style. A "what stands out" box on
page two is written by rules from the numbers, so every department gets
one and nobody writes sixty of them. One template, one parameter, one
loop.

**IPEDS.** One survey file per component, one section per question, the
SQL inside the chunks, checks that print "no errors" or the rows, the
upload file written by the last chunk. The Access database, as a document
that runs.

## Three verbs that are not the same thing

| Verb | Means | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **Run** | execute one chunk, or one line, in the Console, right now; the output appears below the chunk; nothing is written to disk | the green arrow on a chunk; Ctrl+Enter on a line |
| **Render** | execute every chunk from the top in a fresh session and build the output file (HTML, PDF, Word) | the Render button; `quarto render` in the Terminal |
| **Publish** | copy a rendered output somewhere other people can open it | `quarto publish`; or drop the file on a server, SharePoint, the portal |

Run is for thinking. Render is for the document. Publish is for the
audience. A chunk that Runs but does not Render was depending on something
in your session that the document never loaded; Render is the test.

**Source and Visual.** The two buttons at the top left of the editor. Same
file, two views. Source is the plain text: the marks, the fences, the
YAML. Visual looks like a word processor. People write in Visual; an AI
writes Source, because Source is what you paste into it and what it hands
back. Learn to read both. Nothing is lost switching, ever.

# What is inside RStudio

More than R. Point at this page during the tour.

## Languages, in the same document

| Chunk | Runs | Package |
|---|---|---|
| `{r}` | R | |
| `{python}` | Python | `reticulate` |
| `{sql connection=con}` | SQL against a live connection; result becomes a data frame | `DBI`, `odbc` |
| `{ojs}` | Observable JavaScript, interactive in the browser | |
| `{bash}` | shell | |

## Quarto output formats, one line each

`html` `typst` (PDF, nothing to install) `pdf` (LaTeX) `docx` `pptx` `revealjs`
`dashboard` `gfm` (GitHub) and whole websites, books, blogs, manuscripts.
Parameters. Conditional content per format. Cross-references. Citations
with Zotero. `brand.yml` for institutional colors, fonts and logo in one file.

## Packages worth knowing, by job

| Job | Packages |
|---|---|
| Wrangle | `dplyr`, `tidyr`, `janitor`, `stringr`, `lubridate` |
| Tables | `gt` (HTML, PDF, Word), `kableExtra` (PDF), `flextable` (Word, PowerPoint), `reactable`, `DT` (interactive) |
| Charts | `ggplot2`, `patchwork`, `ggrepel`, `plotly` (interactive), `leaflet` (maps) |
| Files | `readxl`, `writexl`, `openxlsx`, `haven` (SAS, SPSS, Stata), `jsonlite`, `httr2` (APIs) |
| Databases | `DBI`, `odbc`, `dbplyr` (write dplyr, get SQL), `keyring` (passwords out of files) |
| Office files | `officer` (build Word and PowerPoint from R) |
| Interactive | `shiny`, Shinylive (Shiny inside a static page) |
| Workflow | Projects, `renv` (lock versions), the Git tab, Terminal, Background Jobs, `styler`, `esquisse` |
| Higher ed | `educationdata` (IPEDS by API), `tidycensus`, `rscorecard`, `IPEDSuploadables` |
| AI | GitHub Copilot (built into RStudio; subscription), `ellmer` (call a model from code), `chattr` |

## Also exists, not covered today

**Shiny** makes interactive dashboards: the reader picks a term or a
college and the page changes. Same `dplyr` and `ggplot2` inside; it needs
a server to run on, which is the cost. Quarto's `dashboard` format and
Shinylive give lighter versions with no server. **Posit Cloud** is RStudio
in a browser; see the note on the first page.

## Publishing

`quarto publish quarto-pub` (free, public). GitHub Pages. Netlify. Posit
Connect (licensed). Drop the HTML on SharePoint. Or what Auburn did: an
Azure static site behind campus sign-in, with a dashboard that shows each
person only the reports they may open.

## How IR offices use this

Fact books as websites. Program review profiles, one per department.
Course evaluation reports, one per instructor. Common Data Set and IPEDS
preparation. Accreditation narratives with the evidence tables embedded.
Survey reports from the Qualtrics API. Retention dashboards. Text analysis
of comments. Feedback reports to feeder institutions, one PDF each.

# Exercise 1: one IPEDS question

*Cecile's segment. A data set, a question, and Quarto to get the answer.*

1. Open `exercises/01_ipeds.qmd`. Click **Render**.
2. Read the file top to bottom. The data set is a CSV of 3,000 invented
   students. The question is quoted from the IPEDS form. The rule is one
   sentence. The chunk filters and counts. The table is the answer.
3. **Try one thing.** Change `attendance == "Full-time"` to
   `"Part-time"`. Render. You just answered a different line.
4. Copy the whole "The answer" section, paste it below itself, change the
   filter again. Two questions, two sections. Thirty questions is the same
   file, longer.

**If you know SQL better than R, this is for you.** Most of the code in
an IPEDS file is SQL. R is the wrapper: it hands the query to the
database, catches the result, and shows it or tests it. The last two
chunks in the file show it: the same count with the data coming from a
warehouse, and the count done in SQL. One chunk, Cecile's shape:

```r
qry <- "
  SELECT academic_period, id, program, degree_code, college, dept
    FROM my_schema.degrees_prelim
   WHERE dept IS NULL OR dept = ''
"
error_dept <- dbGetQuery(con, qry)

if (nrow(error_dept) == 0) {
  cat("No department errors.\n")
} else {
  error_dept
}
```

The SQL is the rule. The `if` is the check. The rendered page shows a
sentence or the rows. Thirty of these is an error report; thirty counting
queries is a survey.

**Access to Oracle to Quarto: what changes.** Cecile's notes from making
the move. The full table is in the primer.

| | Access | Oracle | R / Quarto |
|---|---|---|---|
| Crosstab | `TRANSFORM ... PIVOT` | `PIVOT` | `pivot_wider()` |
| Conditional | `IIf()` | `CASE WHEN` | `if_else()`, `case_when()` |
| Wildcards | `*` `?` | `%` `_` | pattern in `str_detect()` |
| Strings | `"double"` | `'single'` | either |
| Parameter | `[prompt]`, retyped each run | `:bind`, per query | `params$x`, once per document; a file path can be one |
| Comments | a hidden properties box | `--` in the SQL | in the code and in the prose around it |
| One component | 30 min to hours, ~30 queries one by one, stalls on big results | 5 to 15 min, ~10 queries | up to 5 min, all together, output recorded |

A full survey file built this way, with checks that stop the render and
an upload file written by the last chunk, is
`solutions/ipeds_full_template.qmd`.

# Exercise 2: your institution, from the federal data

1. Open `exercises/02_my_institution.qmd`.
2. Near the top, change `unitid: 100858` to your UNITID. The room's are
   in a comment right there.
3. Click **Render**. Read it. Every number came from `data/`; every table
   and chart from a code chunk you can see.
4. Change `format:` at the top to `typst`. Render. A PDF, with nothing
   extra installed. Notice the last section, "Every current program", is
   gone: in the file it is wrapped in
   `::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}`. Long tables for the web,
   short ones for paper, one source. Change it back to `html` when done.

Then look at the file. The YAML block at the top is settings. `params` is
the one thing that changes between institutions. Each grey block is a
chunk; `#| echo: false` hides the code from the reader. Everything else is
Markdown.

## What the data is

The **2026 Program Performance Data (PPD:2026)**, published by the
Department of Education in December 2025, updated January 8, 2026, for the
AHEAD negotiated rulemaking. One row per **institution × credential level
× 4-digit CIP**: 209,321 programs at 5,096 institutions. A preview, for
information only. The official results under STATS (the Student Tuition
and Transparency System, from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act) arrive
**February 2027** at the 6-digit CIP level.

## Three things to know before computing anything

1. **NA means suppressed, not zero.** Fewer than 10 students (16 for
   earnings, 30 for FAFSA-based columns) is blanked. Sums undercount.
2. **Counts of 10 to 19 are shown as 15.** Rates built on them use 15.
3. **The dollars are different years.** Earnings and benchmarks: 2024
   dollars. Debt: 2019 dollars. Yearly aid: nominal.

## The test, in one line

`md_earn_wne_p4` (median earnings of completers working four years after
the 2017-18 and 2018-19 cohorts) against `earn_bnchmrk_cip2_wageb` (high
school graduates aged 25 to 34 in the state for undergraduate programs;
bachelor's holders in the field for graduate programs). Below it:
`earnings_test = "Fail"`.

## The tables in `data/`

| File | One row per | Use for |
|---|---|---|
| `ppd_programs.rds` | program | today: earnings, debt, benchmark, pass/fail, demographics |
| `ppd_yearly.rds` | program × award year | 2015-16 to 2024-25: enrollment, completers, Pell, loans |
| `ppd_cip6_earnings.rds` | program at 6-digit CIP | the earnings detail the official file will use |
| `institutions.csv` | institution | find a UNITID; compare institutions |
| `codebook.csv` | column | every column, what it means, where it came from |

# Exercise 3: the room, one click

1. Open `exercises/03_render_peers.R`. The list is the ten institutions
   in this room, with UNITIDs.
2. Click **Source**. Ten reports appear in `output/`.
3. Edit the list. Change `format` to `"typst"` if you want PDFs. Source
   again.

This is the whole trick behind one-PDF-per-college, one-report-per-
department, one-profile-per-program. The template does not know how many
there are.

## If it breaks

| Message | Means |
|---|---|
| `No programs found for unitid` | typo, or your campus reports under a parent OPEID; search `institutions.csv` by name |
| `could not find function` | a package is not loaded; add `library(...)` in the setup chunk |
| `object 'x' not found` | a chunk above did not run; Render runs them in order from the top |
| the PDF table is cut off | shorten column labels or drop a column; or keep it HTML-only |

## The move

1. Open `02_my_institution.qmd`. Select a chunk, or the whole file. Copy.
2. In the assistant, paste it and ask for **one** change:

> Here is a chunk from a Quarto report in R: *[paste]*. Change it so that
> *[one thing]*. Return only the chunk.

3. Paste the result back over the old chunk. Render.
4. If it fails: "Here is the chunk: *[paste]*. Here is the error:
   *[paste the red text]*. Fix it."

## Pick one thing, then another

- Change the chart colors to my institution's colors (give two hex codes).
- Make the margin chart bars sorted the other way.
- Add a column to the test table showing the margin as a percent.
- Add a bar chart of Pell recipients by year under the enrollment chart.
- Add a section at the end with one sentence summarizing the results.
- Make the at-a-glance table two columns side by side instead of a list.

Each one is five minutes. Finished examples of several are in
`solutions/improvement_examples.qmd`.

## When it answers

Read the code before you paste it. The assistant produces confident code
that runs and is wrong. Rendering is the first test; reading the number is
the second.

# Exercise 5: the report you actually owe someone

Everything so far used our data. This one uses the shape of yours. Think
of one report you produce over and over. Not the hardest; the most
annoying.

1. Write down its column names and types. Not the data. The names. The
   primer's "shape of your data" page has the one-liner for wherever it
   lives: `DESCRIBE` in Oracle, `INFORMATION_SCHEMA` in Snowflake, the
   Database Documenter in Access, `read_excel(n_max = 0)` for a workbook,
   or `shape_of()` in `setup/02_shape_of_my_data.R` for anything already
   in R. You can also ask the assistant to write the metadata query; that
   prompt holds nothing sensitive.
2. In the assistant:

> I produce *[report]* for *[audience]* every *[cadence]*. Today I build
> it in *[Excel / Access / SPSS]* by *[the steps]*. The data has these
> columns: *[names and types, no rows]*. Outline a Quarto document that
> produces it, with a parameter for *[the thing that changes each time]*,
> and write the first two chunks.

3. Make a new file, `my_report.qmd`, in the exercises folder. Paste the
   outline in. Copy the YAML header from `02_my_institution.qmd` on top.
4. Render it with no data. Headings and empty chunks are a plan you can
   take home.

At 11:15 we will put a few plans on the screen.

# Cheat sheet, and taking it home

## The top of a Quarto file

```yaml
---
title: "Report"
date: today
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    embed-resources: true     # one file, images inside
params:
  unitid: 100858
execute:
  echo: false                 # hide code from readers
  warning: false
---
```

## In a chunk

```r
#| label: name          # unique; shows in Render progress
#| fig-height: 4
#| echo: true           # show this one chunk's code
#| eval: false          # show the code, do not run it
```

## Markdown you will use

`# Heading` `## Subheading` `**bold**` `*italic*` `` `code` `` `[text](url)`
`1. list` `- bullet` `| a | b |` for tables, `::: {.callout-note}` for a box,
`` `r params$unitid` `` for a value inside a sentence.

## Render many

```r
quarto::quarto_render("report.qmd", execute_params = list(unitid = 100858),
                      output_file = "Auburn.html")
```

## Connect to your own warehouse (at home)

```r
con <- DBI::dbConnect(odbc::odbc(), dsn = "MY_DSN",
                      UID = "my_user", PWD = keyring::key_get("my_service", "my_user"))
df  <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT ... FROM ...")
```

`MY_DSN` is an ODBC data source your IT office sets up on your machine.
Set the password once in the Console: `keyring::key_set("my_service", "my_user")`.
It is stored by the operating system, not in any file, and never in a
document like this one.

## February 2027

The official STATS file will arrive at 6-digit CIP with its own layout.
In this project, `ingest/make_ppd_tables.R` is the one file that reads the
Department's files. Change it; every report re-renders.
